title: Design: A 31-character term name fits on one row
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have the shop's own active term A whose name is 31 characters long, due 45 days after the invoice date.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom.
  • Open the attached design picture ct-p1-12-a-31-character-term-name.png at 100% zoom beside the screen.
  • Start on the Settings page.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. In the Settings menu, click "Credit Terms".
  2. Resize the browser window to 1536 px wide (for example, maximise it on a 1536 x 864 screen at 100% zoom).
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • In the term A row, term A reads in full on one line, nothing cut off and no dots at the end, in its place among the 45-day terms (as in ct-p1-12-a-31-character-term-name.png).

Step 2:

  • At 1536 px nothing overlaps, nothing is cut off and nothing needs a sideways scroll.
  • The layout described above is unchanged, only wider.

A narrower window than 1440 px may wrap the name onto a second line; it must never be cut off (the design draws only 1440 px).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11670 (Story 1, Credit Terms page and list), story SV-11672 (Story 3, Create or edit a credit term)

  • S1-R15: “Term names are never cut off in the table; a long name wraps onto a second line, with its icons and "Default" tag after it.”
  • S3-R2, Name: “Name (required), focused on open, accepting at most 31 characters, with the hint "Up to 31 characters. Prints on invoices and goes to QuickBooks."”
